title: The Book of the Secrets of Enoch
author: Morfill and Charles (trans)
description: The Book of the Secrets of Enoch (2 Enoch, the Slavonic Enoch), translated from the Slavonic by W. R. Morfill and edited with introduction, notes and indices by R. H. Charles (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1896). Surviving only in Old Church Slavonic manuscripts but probably based on a Jewish or Jewish-Christian work of the first century CE, it recounts Enoch's ascent through seven (in some recensions ten) heavens, guided by two angels. He sees the prisons of the fallen angels, paradise and hell, the courses of the sun and moon, and finally the face of the Lord, before being transformed and instructed in the secrets of creation, including a cosmogony that describes creation from the invisible through the great aeon Adoil. Enoch returns to teach his sons, then is taken up, and the text closes with the story of Methuselah and the miraculous birth of Melchizedek. It is a key source on heavenly ascent and Enochic cosmology.
